# M8: Mount the fuse post

> *Mount the fuse post in the D shaped hole in the rear of the chassis. The rubber washer goes between the chassis outside and the shoulder of the fuse post. Fasten with nut provided and position lugs as shown in pictorial.* — manual page 5

## What you're doing physically

The kit supplies a **panel-mount fuse holder** — a cylindrical assembly that holds one standard 3AG fuse (1¼" long, ¼" diameter glass). It mounts through the **D-shaped hole** on the rear of the chassis.

Assembly from outside in:

1. Rubber washer over the fuse post body.
2. Insert the post into the D-shaped hole from outside.
3. From inside, thread the supplied hex nut onto the post and tighten.

The D-shape (a flat side on one edge of an otherwise circular hole) keys the fuse post so it can't rotate. Without the D-shape, the post would spin loose every time someone tightens or loosens it to change the fuse.

Position the two solder lugs on the inner end of the post per the pictorial — typically with one lug oriented up and one down for clean wire routing.

## What the fuse does

The fuse sits in series with the **mains line** (hot wire). If the amp ever shorts internally (a tube goes catastrophically gassy, a filter cap shorts, etc.) and starts drawing far more current than normal, the fuse melts and disconnects mains — preventing fire, transformer damage, or worse.

The kit specifies a **3 A slow-blow** fuse. "Slow-blow" means the fuse tolerates brief high-current transients (like the in-rush at power-on as caps charge and transformers magnetize) without blowing, but a sustained overcurrent will still pop it. A fast-blow fuse at 3 A would nuisance-trip on power-on.

## Why the rubber washer

The rubber washer between the chassis exterior and the fuse post's shoulder:

1. **Seals** the hole against dust and moisture.
2. **Insulates** — adds a layer of rubber between the chassis edge and the fuse post body (the fuse post body is electrically hot when the fuse blows because it's directly connected to mains).
3. **Strain relief** — the rubber compresses slightly when the nut is tightened, locking the post position against vibration.
